h1:
Surin Isan Eats
Som Tam, Larb, Koi & Grilled Chicken — 10 Spots Locals Eat At
intro: Surin is a Lower Isan town where the food runs seriously fiery, because people here eat som tam, larb and koi as an everyday thing. The province even holds som tam pounding contests often enough that you'll find a regional-champion shop right in town. We picked the places that Surin locals talk about and that real reviews back up, sorted so you can choose by the flavor you're after — heavy-handed som tam shops, raw-beef larb and koi soi ju joints, and charcoal grilled chicken.

blocks.html: Isan food isn't exactly exotic for visitors, but the fun part is that Surin genuinely has a regional-champion som tam shop right in town, plus raw-beef larb and koi soi ju joints where people eat beef nearly raw, the Lower Isan way. We've ordered the list by local reputation, how consistent the reviews are, and how easy each spot is to drop into, with the neighborhood and a rough price so you can match the right place to the right meal.

One honest note up front: this ranking isn't a hard verdict on who's tastier than whom, because bold flavor comes down to each person's palate. A few former champions have reviews grumbling that the taste has shifted a bit across generations and seasons. So we cover both the strengths and the things worth knowing, the way reviewers describe them — read through and pick the shop that matches your mood that day.

blocks.text: 10 Surin Isan spots locals actually eat at

items.name: Som Tam Phet Mani Branch 1
items.blurb: An old-guard som tam shop in Surin that's been open so long it's now run by the third generation, and once took first place for som tam in all of Isan. It's a two-unit shophouse with seating downstairs and up. The house mixed som tam stands out for its savory depth from dried shrimp, roasted peanuts and pla ra (fermented fish), and the grilled chicken is done fresh daily. The most-ordered dishes are pork aom, tam sua and the mixed som tam. Some reviews say the flavor has changed a touch over time, but it's still the first name people think of for som tam in Surin.
items.meta: Lak Mueang Rd · town center, Mueang Surin · open roughly 9am–evening
items.price: Som tam from ฿40–60 · around ฿100–250 per person

items.name: Je Tuk Som Tam
items.blurb: Another regular haunt for Surin locals, over on Krung Si Nai Rd near Municipal School 3. The standout is its own recipe of cooked, boiled pla ra — fragrant and clean — which once won a prize at a Surin som tam contest. The som tam goes in with both dried and fresh chilies for a fully loaded kick, balanced with fresh papaya, long beans, bitter melon and hog plum. Another highlight is the lemongrass grilled chicken roasted in a clay pot. Closed Mondays.
items.meta: Krung Si Nai Rd · near Municipal School 3, Mueang Surin · noon–8pm, closed Mon
items.price: Som tam from ฿40–60 · grilled chicken around ฿100

items.name: Ran Tam Kathoey
items.blurb: A som tam and larb spot in town that stays open into the evening and is packed almost every day, on Thetsaban 1 Rd. The standout dishes include a bold crab-and-pla-ra som tam, grilled chicken, spicy tom saap with soft cartilage, pork larb, fried pla som, and pork belly fried with fish sauce. It's the kind of place where you sit down, order a spread and share — an easy choice when locals are meeting up for dinner.
items.meta: 353/7 Thetsaban 1 Rd · town center, Mueang Surin · roughly 10:30am–9pm
items.price: Som tam & larb from ฿45–70 · around ฿100–200 per person

items.name: Larb Lung Sit Surin
items.blurb: A raw-beef larb and koi joint that Isan diehards in Surin love, over near the May Wholesale market. The flavor is fierce and goes right to the spot. Repeat orders are the slow-stewed beef hot pot, koi suea kua, soi ju, and grilled cow's udder. It's for people who eat beef the serious Lower Isan way — but if raw beef isn't your thing, you can order cooked larb or kua koi instead.
items.price: Larb & koi from ฿60–80 · hot pot by size

items.name: Larb Koi Khrua Khun Mia
items.blurb: A larb and koi shop near the Ton Pho junction that Surin locals praise for its savory larb and koi. Comfortable seating, and you can order larb, koi and tom saap with sticky rice for a big shared meal — great for a group ordering to share. The plus is it's easy to find, right in town.
items.price: Larb & koi from ฿50–70 · tom saap from ฿60

items.name: Ma Mao Larb Koi
items.blurb: A larb-koi and made-to-order spot that covers both the spicy-Isan crowd and plain home-style dishes under one roof. Ideal for a group where some people can handle heat and some can't — order larb and koi for the spice lovers, then made-to-order dishes for the milder eaters, all at the same table.
items.price: Larb & koi from ฿50–70 · made-to-order from ฿50

items.name: Som Tam Kim Lang
items.blurb: A som tam shop in town with a very long menu — lots of som tam styles plus various stir-fry dishes. Reviewers like that you can order a full range in one place, so it's great for people who want to try a bit of everything, from tam Thai and crab-pla-ra som tam to drinking-snack dishes.
items.price: Som tam from ฿40–60 · stir-fry dishes to order

items.name: Som Tam Footpath
items.blurb: A som tam stall in town that Surin locals know well — heavy-handed pounding in the local style, friendly prices. Good for an afternoon snack or takeaway. It's a street spot where regulars swing by for a quick plate of som tam and a skewer of grilled chicken.
items.price: Som tam from around ฿40 · grilled chicken from ฿60 per skewer

items.name: Khon Mak Tam By Kapaeng
items.blurb: A bold, fiery som tam shop focused on lots of som tam styles loaded with toppings. Reviewers point to the savory depth of the crab-pla-ra som tam and tam sua. It's for people who like a packed mortar with a full-on flavor hit, with fried and grilled add-ons to round it into a meal with sticky rice.
items.price: Som tam from ฿45–65 · fried/grilled dishes from ฿60

items.name: Salt-Grilled Free-Range Chicken, Talat Noi Ruenrom
items.blurb: A grilled chicken spot Surin locals talk about for its salt-grilled, charcoal-cooked free-range chicken — firm meat, fragrant skin, eaten with jaew dipping sauce, sticky rice and som tam. It's old-school grilled chicken, perfect to grab and pair with som tam from a nearby shop to round out a proper spicy spread.
items.meta: Talat Noi Ruenrom area · Mueang Surin
items.price: Grilled chicken from around ฿80–150 per whole/half bird

blocks.title: How to order it spicy but right for you
blocks.html: If you can't handle heavy heat, say “prik noi” (light on chili) when you order, because Isan shops in Surin pound it heavy-handed to local taste. As for soi ju and koi suea, those are semi-raw beef — if you're not used to it, order cooked larb or kua koi instead and you'll still get the same Lower Isan flavor, just easier on the stomach.

blocks.text: Pick a spot by the meal you want

blocks.html: Isan food in Surin works for lots of moments in the day, from an afternoon snack to a long, lingering dinner with friends. Choose by the situation so you don't end up at the wrong shop for the wrong meal.

items: Afternoon snack / takeaway — a stall like Footpath; order a single plate of som tam with a skewer of grilled chicken for a light, cheap fill.
Want championship-level som tam — Phet Mani 1 or Je Tuk, two old-guard som tam shops with award pedigrees; get the grilled chicken on the side too.
Long beef-focused dinner — Larb Lung Sit or Khrua Khun Mia; order larb, koi, soi ju and a hot pot to share with sticky rice.
A group with different spice levels — Ma Mao Larb Koi or Tam Kathoey; both have spicy dishes and easy-going food under one roof.

blocks.text: Know the Lower Isan flavors before you order

blocks.html: If you're not too familiar with the Isan menu, these are the staples almost every Surin shop has — order along these lines and you won't go wrong. Lower Isan also has raw-beef dishes like soi ju and koi suea as a signature that's hard to find in other regions.

items.name: Crab & pla ra som tam
items.blurb: Pounded in the mortar with fermented fish and salted crab — the bold, intense version locals order most. If it's too hot for you, switch to tam Thai with dried shrimp.

items.name: Larb & koi
items.blurb: Larb is tossed with toasted rice, chili powder and kaffir lime leaf; koi is beef or pork tossed with sour-spicy seasoning. Lower Isan favors koi suea kua, semi-cooked.

items.name: Soi ju
items.blurb: Fresh sliced beef dipped in hot jaew sauce with boiled offal — a Lower Isan way of eating beef. If you're not used to it, order it cooked instead.

items.name: Grilled chicken / tom saap
items.blurb: Charcoal grilled chicken with fragrant skin to eat with som tam, while tom saap with soft cartilage is a bold, sour broth to cut the richness — best sipped hot.

faq.q: Which som tam shop in Surin is the standout?
faq.a: Som Tam Phet Mani 1 in the town center is an old-guard shop that once took first place for som tam in all of Isan, and Je Tuk, which uses its own recipe of cooked boiled pla ra, is another som tam place Surin locals visit regularly. Both have good grilled chicken to order alongside.

faq.q: Where do I go in Surin for raw-beef larb, koi and soi ju?
faq.a: Larb Lung Sit near the May Wholesale market is the raw-beef spot Isan fans love, with koi suea kua, soi ju and slow-stewed beef hot pot. Khrua Khun Mia at the Ton Pho junction is a comfortable in-town larb-koi shop that's good for sharing.

faq.q: Is Surin Isan food very spicy?
faq.a: Most of it is pounded heavy-handed to local taste. If you can't take heavy heat, say “prik noi” (light on chili) when you order — the shops will adjust — and choosing tam Thai instead of crab-pla-ra som tam will be milder.

faq.q: What are soi ju and koi suea — are they eaten raw?
faq.a: Soi ju is fresh sliced beef dipped in jaew sauce, eaten with boiled offal, while koi suea kua is semi-cooked seasoned beef. It's a Lower Isan way of eating beef. If raw isn't for you, order cooked larb or kua koi instead for a similar flavor.

faq.q: Roughly how much does Surin Isan food cost?
faq.a: Prices are mostly friendly: som tam and larb start around ฿40–80, grilled chicken from around ฿80–150 per whole/half bird, and a filling meal for two runs about ฿200–350 depending on whether you add beef dishes like soi ju or a hot pot.
